v.rationale: All three solve the main traps: JSON 401 for scripts without an Accept header (redirectGuestsTo returns null), a generic 404 body that hides 'No query results for model [App\Models\Order]', the same 404 for foreign and missing orders, user_id that cannot be mass-assigned, and 201 from a JsonResource on a newly created model. The ranking turns on bugs. impl-1 is the only one that thought about middleware order: by putting CheckAbilities ahead of SubstituteBindings it guarantees 403 for a token without the ability, and it tests this. Probes found no bugs. impl-2 avoids the ordering problem by scoping the query through the relationship (simple and idiomatic), but it leaves out the integer cast, so form-encoded creates echo total_cents back as a string; it also carries some test noise and an unused alias. impl-3 has the best test suite and nice touches such as the composite index, but probes confirmed that a write-only token gets 404 for a missing order (should be 403) and 403 for another user's existing order. That breaks the 403 requirement and leaks which order IDs exist, and that is the task's main concern.
